dialogues.speaker: Firsova
dialogues.text: *sigh*... This is already the fifth time this month. What on earth is going wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Dementieva
dialogues.text: Please don't sigh, milady. You're both kind and lovely. If there's a problem, then the problem must lie with the men you've been matched with.

dialogues.speaker: Firsova
dialogues.text: But... our conversations in the dining car always seem to go well. Why is it that after drinking the tea you serve them, they suddenly turn pale and flee the train?

dialogues.speaker: Dementieva
dialogues.text: Indeed. Why is that? I've been trying to figure it out myself.

dialogues.speaker: Dementieva
dialogues.text: Look, you're drinking the very same tea right now...

dialogues.speaker: Firsova
dialogues.text: There's nothing wrong with the tea.

dialogues.speaker: Dementieva
dialogues.text: Exactly. Which means that man was simply far too frail. How could someone like that ever be worthy of someone as perfect as you?

dialogues.speaker: Firsova
dialogues.text: W—Well, when you put it that way... But if this keeps happening, when am I ever going to get married?

dialogues.speaker: Firsova
dialogues.text: Father has been pressing me about it... We've traveled for so long, and I've practically met every pure-blooded Domovoy noble in Snezhnaya...

dialogues.speaker: Dementieva
dialogues.text: There's no need to worry, milady. Even if every dull, disappointing man in all of Snezhnaya lets you down, I will always remain by your side and take care of you.

dialogues.speaker: Firsova
dialogues.text: Mm... Having you with me really does make me feel much more at ease.

dialogues.speaker: Dementieva
dialogues.text: Hehe, hearing you say that is the greatest honor I could ask for.
